question: What does 21 CFR 820.10 say?
answer_raw: 21 CFR 820.10 requires a manufacturer subject to this part to document a quality management system that complies with ISO 13485 and other applicable requirements. The manufacturer must document a system to assign unique device identification in accordance with part 830 of this chapter, document procedures for traceability in accordance with part 821 of this chapter, and notify FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of part 803 of this chapter. Advisory notices shall be handled in accordance with part 806 of this chapter. The requirements apply to devices automated with computer software, devices listed in the following table, and devices that support or sustain life. If applicable, the requirements apply to devices that support or sustain life. The enforcement of these requirements renders a device adulterated under section 501(h) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. [4][5]

21 CFR 820.10 requires a manufacturer subject to this part to document a quality management system that complies with ISO 13485 and other applicable requirements. Advisory notices shall be handled in accordance with part 806 of this chapter. The requirements apply to devices automated with computer software, devices listed in the following table, and devices that support or sustain life. If applicable, the requirements apply to devices that support or sustain life. The enforcement of these requirements renders a device adulterated under section 501(h) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act. [4][5]

question: What are the tamper-evident packaging requirements for OTC drug products?
answer_raw:
What are the tamper-evident packaging requirements for OTC drug products?  

The tamper-evident packaging requirements for OTC drug products are outlined in 21 CFR 211.132(b), which states that the requirements will improve the security of OTC drug packaging and help assure the safety and effectiveness of OTC drug products.  

The requirements also include that the tamper-evident packaging feature must be placed in a way that is unaffected if the feature is breached or missing, as stated in 21 CFR 211.132(c)(1)(iii). Additionally, the packaging must identify all tamper-evident feature(s) and any capsule sealing technologies used to comply with paragraph (b) of this section, as stated in 21 CFR 211.132(c)(1)(i).

answer_raw:
The EU Medical Device Regulation requires that UDI (Unique Device Identification) must be assigned to a device under the following conditions:  
- Non-Device-MDDS must be assigned to a device under section 201(h) of the FD&C Act, and UDI must be assigned to a device that is a hardware function intended to assist software functions.  
- Device-MDDS must be assigned to a device under section 201(h) of the FD&C Act, and UDI must be assigned to a device that is a hardware function intended to assist the software functions listed in the recommendations.

answer_raw: [1] §820.10(b)(3) requires that the manufacturer must notify the FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of part 803 of this chapter. [3] If applicable, the manufacturer must also document a system to assign a UDI to the subject device and utilization of UDI to identify devices accurately from manufacturing through distribution to patient use, as required by 21 CFR 820.10(b)(1) and 21 CFR part 830. [7] The submitter should also document a system to assign UDI to the medical device in accordance with the requirements of 21 CFR 820.10(b)(2), 21 CFR part 821, and Subclause 7.5.9.1. [7] The process by which the submitter will notify FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of 21 CFR 820.10(b)(3) and 21 CFR part 803, as set forth at Subclause 8.2.3, is required. [7] The manufacturer must also include a summary of the MDR procedure(s) and explain how this process is linked
answer:
[1] §820.10(b)(3) requires that the manufacturer must notify the FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of part 803 of this chapter. [3] If applicable, the manufacturer must also document a system to assign a UDI to the subject device and utilization of UDI to identify devices accurately from manufacturing through distribution to patient use, as required by 21 CFR 820.10(b)(1) and 21 CFR part 830. The submitter should also document a system to assign UDI to the medical device in accordance with the requirements of 21 CFR 820.10(b)(2), 21 CFR part 821, and Subclause 7.5.9.1. The process by which the submitter will notify FDA of complaints that meet the reporting criteria of 21 CFR 820.10(b)(3) and 21 CFR part 803, as set forth at Subclause 8.2.3, is required. The manufacturer must also include a summary of the MDR procedure(s) and explain how this process is linked
